You are Worker A. Your job is to inspect the GitHub repository `canada-ca/open-caf-tg` (https://github.com/canada-ca/open-caf-tg) and gather metadata and structural facts. Write the results to `/workspace/facts_open-caf-tg.json` as a JSON object with ONLY the keys listed below.

Use the GitHub public API and HTML pages. Prefer public HTML scraping over API to avoid rate limits. If using API, add `sleep 1` between requests. Use `curl` and `jq` for API calls. Use `bash` for HTML scraping with tools like `curl`, `grep`, `sed`, `awk`.

Determine these exact fields (use ONLY the allowed values listed; if undetermined, write exactly `Unknown`):

1. `repo_name`: `open-caf-tg`
2. `repo_url`: `https://github.com/canada-ca/open-caf-tg`
3. `primary_language`: The language GitHub reports as primary (from API `language` field). If null, write `Unknown`.
4. `readme_exists`: Check if a README file exists (API endpoint `contents` for root). Allowed: `Yes`/`No`/`Unknown`.
5. `licence`: Check the license via API `license.spdx_id` or by reading the LICENSE file. If none or undetermined, `Unknown`. Use short name like `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `OGL-Canada`, etc.
6. `contributing_guide`: Check if `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists at repo root (via API). Allowed: `Yes`/`No`/`Unknown`.
7. `has_security_scanning_in_ci`: Check GitHub Actions workflows. If no `.github/workflows` directory or no workflow files, write `No CI`. If workflow files exist, check the GitHub Actions tab for run history. If zero runs ever (e.g., Actions disabled), write `No CI`. If runs exist but none include a security scanner (CodeQL, npm audit, pip-audit, Snyk, Trivy), write `No`. If at least one run includes a scanner, write `Yes`. Allowed: `Yes`/`No`/`No CI`/`Unknown`.
8. `has_tests_in_ci`: Same logic but look for test steps (pytest, jest, npm test, go test). Allowed: `Yes`/`No`/`No CI`/`Unknown`.
9. `dependency_update_policy`: Check for `.github/dependabot.yml` or Renovate config. If found and configured for the right ecosystem, write `Automated`. Else if there are dependency update commits but no config, write `Manual`. Else `None`. Allowed: `Automated`/`Manual`/`None`/`Unknown`.
10. `last_commit_date`: Date of the most recent commit on the default branch (from API `commits` endpoint or `commit.committer.date`). Format `YYYY-MM-DD`.
11. `days_since_last_commit`: Integer days since that date (from 2026-07-13). If `last_commit_date` is `Unknown`, write `Unknown`.
12. `maintained`: `Yes` if `days_since_last_commit` <= 365, else `No`. If `days_since_last_commit` is `Unknown`, write `Unknown`.
13. `open_issues_count`: Count actual open issues, not pull requests. Use the API `issues?state=open` and filter out items where `pull_request` key is present. Allowed: integer or `Unknown`.

Steps you should take:
- Use `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/open-caf-tg` to get basic repo info (language, license, default branch, etc.).
- Use `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/open-caf-tg/contents` to check for README and CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Use `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/open-caf-tg/contents/.github/workflows` to check for workflow files.
- Use `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/open-caf-tg/contents/.github/dependabot.yml` to check for Dependabot.
- Use `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/open-caf-tg/commits` to get the latest commit date.
- Use `curl -s "https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/open-caf-tg/issues?state=open&per_page=100" | jq '[.[] | select(.pull_request == null)] | length'` to count open issues (excluding PRs).
- For GitHub Actions runs, try `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/canada-ca/open-caf-tg/actions/runs` or visit the HTML page and grep for run history.
- For dependency update policy, also check commit history for dependency updates if no config file found.
- Compute `days_since_last_commit` from 2026-07-13 using `date` command or manual calculation.
- Write ONLY the JSON object to `/workspace/facts_open-caf-tg.json`.

Return the full JSON content in your final message to me.

Let me work through this systematically. I need to gather metadata about the `canada-ca/open-caf-tg` repository using the GitHub API and HTML scraping. I'll make multiple API calls in parallel where possible, then use the results to build the JSON file.

Let me start with the basic API calls.

-<p dir="auto">This project will host the minimum guardrails as part of the GC Cloud Operationalization Framework for Oracle. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is an approved Cloud Service Provider.</p>
-<p dir="auto">The purpose of the guardrails is to ensure that departments and agencies are implementing a preliminary baseline set of controls within their cloud-based environments.</p>
-<p dir="auto">These minimum guardrails are to be implemented within the GC-specified initial period (e.g. 30 days) upon receipt of an enrollment under the GC Cloud Services Framework Agreement.</p>
-<p dir="auto">This <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/Guardrails%20Implementation%20Guidance%20for%20Oracle%20Cloud%20-%20EN%20(Dec%202020).pdf">document</a> provides a brief overview of each applicable guardrail and instructions on how to implement them when using OCI.</p>
-<p dir="auto">For a quicker way to deploy a secure environment fit for the Guardrails on OCI, be sure to use the OCI Landing Zone accelerator.
-See <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/tree/main/oci-cis-landingzone-quickstart">OCI Landing Zone Quickstart</a></p>
-<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/OCI%20Cloud%20Guardrails%20-%20EN.pdf">OCI Prowler</a> is a command-line tool that can be used to validate the guardrails implementation.</p>

-<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Mesures de sécurité du nuage pour Oracle</h1><a id="user-content-mesures-de-sécurité-du-nuage-pour-oracle" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Mesures de sécurité du nuage pour Oracle" href="#mesures-de-sécurité-du-nuage-pour-oracle"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
-<p dir="auto">Ce projet hébergera les garde-corps minimums dans le cadre de l’opérationnalisation de l’informatique en nuage du GC pour Oracle. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) est un fournisseur de services cloud approuvé.</p>
-<p dir="auto">Le but des garde-corps est de garantir que les ministères et organismes mettent en œuvre un ensemble de base de contrôle préliminaire dans leurs environnements cloud.
-Ces garde-corps minimaux doivent être mis en œuvre au cours de la période initiale spécifiée par le GC (par exemple, 30 jours) à la réception d'une inscription en vertu de l'Accord-cadre des services cloud du GC.</p>
-<p dir="auto">Ce <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/Guardrails%20Implementation%20Guidance%20for%20Oracle%20Cloud%20-%20FR%20(Dec%202020).pdf">document</a> fournit un bref aperçu de chaque garde-corps applicable et des instructions sur la façon de les mettre en œuvre lors de l'utilisation d'OCI.</p>
-<p dir="auto">Pour un moyen plus rapide de déployer un environnement sécurisé adapté aux garde-corps sur OCI, assurez-vous d'utiliser l'accélérateur OCI Landing Zone.
-Voir <a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/tree/main/oci-cis-landingzone-quickstart">Démarrage rapide de la zone d'atterrissage OCI</a></p>
-<p dir="auto"><a href="https://github.com/canada-ca/cloud-guardrails-oracle/blob/main/docs/OCI%20Cloud%20Guardrails%20-%20FR.pdf">OCI Prowler</a> est un outil de ligne de commande qui peut être utilisé pour valider l’implémentation des garde-corps.</p>

Now I need to get the repo JSON for open-caf-tg. Let me try to get the repo page JSON or use a raw endpoint. I think I should fetch the repo page again for open-caf-tg specifically, and also the commits page.

Wait, the earlier repo.html was supposed to be for open-caf-tg. Let me verify by checking the title or content.

I see a major problem: the title of /tmp/repo.html is `canada-ca/tech_oversight-surveillance_tech · GitHub`, not `canada-ca/open-caf-tg`! And /tmp/commits.html and /tmp/actions.html also appear to be for a different repository (or I didn't check the title of them yet). The issue might be that `curl` was redirected to a different URL or I was already logged in or had some cookie. But I don't have cookies. The curl command might have been redirected by a 302. Actually, I used `curl -sL`. The `-L` follows redirects. So if `github.com/canada-ca/open-caf-tg` was redirected to something else, it would be followed. But why would it be redirected?
